source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It turns current treatment preferences into actionable medical orders in addition to an advance directive; state availability varies.","B":"It is mainly for healthy adults planning far ahead and replaces the advance directive once it is signed.","C":"It records values for future discussion but does not function as a medical order during an emergency.","D":"Use a standard POLST form across states because the resulting clinical orders remain portable once they are signed by the appropriate clinician."}}
source_row.rationale: NIH/NIA explains that POLST/MOLST forms provide guidance that healthcare professionals can act on immediately in an emergency and serve as medical orders in addition to an advance directive. They are generally used for people who are seriously ill or near the end of life, and patients should check their state because availability and form vary.
